verdicts.reason: A is a proper vertical rebuild: headline, then phone, then a large CTA. Its flaws are the left-aligned headline sitting against the centred phone and CTA, and the fine print promoted to sit under the headline. B shrinks the phone and leaves a huge dead gap above a tiny CTA crammed bottom-left, so the CTA is buried and the bottom third is wasted.

A puts the phone above the headline, which weakens the reading order. Its headline, subtext and CTA are packed into one cramped cluster with empty space above and below, and the left-aligned text clashes with the centred CTA. B leads with the headline, has a well-sized phone and a dominant CTA; its only issues are the mixed left/centre axis and the fine print moved up.

A has a clear headline, product and CTA sequence with good scale; minor flaws are the mixed alignment and the fine print sitting high. B shrinks the phone to a near-invisible icon jammed beside a small CTA at the very bottom, leaves a vast empty top third, and loses the key product imagery.

A shrinks the phone to a small icon at the top, so the product becomes trivial. It also leaves an awkward gap above the CTA and dead space at the bottom, and the left-aligned headline clashes with the centred CTA. B keeps the phone prominent, has a clear hierarchy and a strong centred CTA; it needs only polish on alignment and fine-print placement.
